opportunities.title: Historic buildings and structures grant

amount.raw: Generally, £1,000 to £30,000 (average approx. £15,000). Sometimes larger sums are considered.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charities, organisations with exempt charitable status, recognised public bodies, Community Benefit Societies, and CICs limited by guarantee. Project must be UK based, not complete, and focus on a listed building or structure.
opportunities.summary: Funds the preservation, conservation and repair of listed historic buildings, structures and architectural features, giving special consideration to those helping find sustainable solutions for conservation and re-use, especially buildings at risk and of outstanding importance. Covers project costs, staff costs, fees, internships, initial exploratory work and capital costs.

opportunities.title: Places of worship grant
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Anglican churches must apply via the ChurchCare conservation grants scheme (part-funded by the Trust); all other denominations, faiths and cathedrals may apply directly to the Trust. Repair grants are no longer provided to places of worship open for active worship.
opportunities.summary: Funds the conservation of historic interiors and historic objects in places of worship open for regular worship, including bells, books and manuscripts, clocks, decorative plasterwork, metalwork and church plate, monuments, organs, paintings, stained glass, textiles, timberwork, wall paintings and historic structures in churchyards, plus commissioning of conservation reports.

opportunities.title: Conservation of cultural heritage grant
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charities, organisations with exempt charitable status, recognised public bodies, Community Benefit Societies and CICs limited by guarantee, provided they are not eligible for the grant programmes run by AIM and NMCT. Project must be UK based and not complete.
opportunities.summary: Funds the preservation and conservation of culturally and historically significant collections and objects, including works of art, books, significant ephemera, artefacts and archives. Conservation work should be carried out by an accredited conservator, informed by a conservation report, and enable greater public access. Supports paid internships and knowledge-sharing.

opportunities.title: Archives Revealed
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charities, organisations with exempt charitable status, and recognised public bodies. Project must be UK based and not complete.
opportunities.summary: Partnership funding programme between The National Archives, The National Lottery Heritage Fund, the Pilgrim Trust and the Wolfson Foundation. It is the only UK grant programme dedicated to cataloguing and unlocking archival collections, ensuring significant archives representing the lives and perspectives of all people across the UK are made accessible to the public. Applications are made via the National Archives website.
